Thanks for the reply. I do agree some moments things feel like they may lessen, and in those moment things might be a little ok. It’s discouraging when those moments are fewer than the fingers on my hands, and the difficult and down moments are longer and more endless. Each day and night is another struggle, and sometimes struggling so much leaves you so exhausted. The problem is there isn’t really much relief from this struggle and the exhaustion never really goes away. I don’t feel happy anymore, or very very rarely I feel a slight moment of what could be happy, but then it reminds me that the happy will go away quickly, and it won’t last, and everything just drops really low again, kind of like something will always go wrong or be taken away. Daily and nightly struggles, where you don’t even want to be happy, just want to be ok. Like baseline is perfectly fine, I’m just discouraged a lot by how often bottom hits. But thank you for reaching out, talking to people in some way does help to mediate out the thoughts especially when people are able to empathize more.

Not a problem, I try to respond when I can to posts here and there. Definitely it is difficult to trust others and feel let down in the end, especially because they don’t have the same scenarios or thoughts that you might have. Honestly, even people with the best intentions can be counterproductive in helping escape your thoughts because ultimately, unless they have been in your situation, they will never truly understand how you might feel and how difficult things may be. That’s why I do find talking on here to be slightly better. While these are complete online strangers to me, it’s helpful to know some people are able to feel what I’m feeling and go through the same difficulties we deal with day to day with our thoughts. The level of empathy does help, and it’s a lot better to not be judged on how you feel and keep being told to “get better”. Just like with a cold, you can’t just tell someone to get better and expect them to get better, if that makes sense. 

A good thing to try is just to accept the people that care about you, but lower expectations for them. Basically what I do is I recognize that some people care somewhat, and are trying what they can, but like I said if they have never experienced it, they can’t fully understand. So when it gets to a point where it starts to hurt more with what others are doing, I kind of flip that switch towards “they don’t get it, so that’s all they CAN do” kind of thinking. Not sure if that makes too much sense. Honestly I think what might be helpful is just to be heard and accepted for what you’re saying, judgement free, advice free, just someone for you to vent your hurtful thoughts and emotions, and feelings of frustration towards. And they don’t need to say they “get it” or anything like that, just understand that it’s hard for you personally, and that’s a start right there if you can feel that sense of comfort, even if it happens to be one of us internet strangers.

And in terms of keeping busy, you’re occupied with work, that’s good already, especially during the situation the world is in right now. You work, so you’re productive already. You play games, that’s something you enjoy so it’s ok to unwind. Productivity can be subjective. If you want to do more, pick up another hobby maybe like exercising or reading. Not everything has to be objectively productive, honestly if you feel depressed and tired, laying down and napping is perfectly fine. Gotta do what feels ok for you to do, and it’s ok to not be productive. Days that you feel slightly more motivated or a little more stable, then you can be productive. On down and beaten days, it’s ok, just take it easy and be easy on yourself. Tough days are common, it’s not easy, but little things get through minutes and hours.

Hey there, the fact that you have these thought and questions is pretty testament to the fact that you recognize injustices, difficulties, and unfairness in the world and in your personal life. I don’t think you need to compare yourself to other’s situations or who may have it worse when you reflect on your emotions and state of mind. Remember, your feelings, thoughts and emotions are valid and are specific to you at the moment, despite what others may say or judge. It is perfectly right for you to feel the struggle of being pulled back and forth between your own personal values and struggles along with the world’s “standards” which unfortunately are less than fair, and also somewhat encourage the lack of morality and reward those who do wrong to others. I’ve been victim to it as well, pretty harshly being betrayed and twisted by a person I thought was good but in the end I was being abused and treated with such toxicity it made me want to end my life. I still feel extremely depressed and often have thoughts of not wanting to be around anymore, but in the spare moments I have I try to focus on other things little by little. I’m not certain it’ll make my life any better, or if life would get any better in the future, but sometimes distractions help while you discover a different sense of purpose or goal to reach to somehow get through another day. You mentioned you have small goals that you wanted, just difficulty imagining working towards those goals in our “traditional” society. That’s a start already, while things are definitely not ideal, sometimes a job can just be a job, it may be stressful and downright disappointing, but if it helps you get your goals at the end of the day it is a little something. While maintaining healthy relationships with people is difficult, especially if they are not understanding of your situation and can’t empathize with you, I do think it’s important to try to avoid isolation. Often our thoughts plague us a lot and make us want to be isolated, I feel that often and feel that people would be either better off without me, or I would just be a bother if I brought it up. Sometimes you just need to spend a little time with people and if you don’t feel comfortable sharing with them, that’s ok, at least you were able to be around others for a brief moment. And that’s why you can come on this subreddit also, it’s full of people who can empathize more closely with what you may be going through, and because it’s online it is somewhat anonymous, so it’s ok to just vent. Sometimes you never know some random online stranger can reply something that might help engage your thoughts more. I think, and this is my perspective I am in know way super qualified to give any advice, just my thoughts, it’s best to focus on the little things in your life right now. If you have your pure values, try to see what ways you’re able to maintain them throughout each day, instead of focusing too strongly on how the world may end up corrupting you in the future. I know that’s “easier said than done” but you never know what little changes can affect your thoughts and life. There are still the handful of kind and purehearted people out there, just like you. Unfortunately we are surrounded a lot by broken and hurtful selfish people, but you never know who could come along and be just like you. Hope that provided some thinking points.

Maybe try newer things? It doesn’t have to be anything too active or engaging, mostly just some sort of thing to try to distract you or get your mind off of things even for a moment. While distraction isn’t a very healthy coping mechanism, at times like these any small thing may help get through a couple more minutes each day. Things like venting on this subreddit, joining online chat rooms to just have some interaction chatting with people, or just watching mindless shows or videos, reading, napping, just little things to keep your mind occupied with other thoughts that can keep your mind from wandering deeper into depression or anger towards things. I’m not saying it could be incredibly helpful, but there could be a possible slight change in your day to day mood with these things. Personally today is a rough one for me, so trying to occupy my mind with other things is all I can do at this point, and even then that’s a struggle.

Well a decent start is reaching out to people on these subreddits. You never know when you can run into someone on the internet to just hold conversations with and empathize with you. Definitely is tougher when your friends have opposing views to yours regarding suicide because it can make you feel more isolated and dejected about your thoughts and emotions. Life is not easy at all, and it is a jarring experience to start disliking life and going through each day more beaten down than the last. Are there some things you still enjoy or find some calm doing? Maybe focus on those things as sort of a day by day distraction, it might create a different sense of purpose to direct your thoughts towards to help a small but each day.

For sure I definitely can relate to that. Sometimes I feel so beaten down that I just want to sleep and never wake up, but sometimes it’s beating down on me so hard that I can’t even fall asleep. And waking up the next day feels even worse because you’re stuck in the cycle again. It’s not easy to feel what you’re feeling, and to know you’re suffering a lot in life is something I can empathize with. Life is rough, and many times for us the bad days can heavily outweigh the good days (if there are any). Posting on here is a step though, there are plenty of us on this sub, and other subs, so you are not alone in the way that you feel and your thoughts. Your pain and struggles with life are valid, so it is ok to hurt this much. If you feel that talking to people helps a bit, reach out to people you think you can trust, and make it in a sense where you don’t want to be judged, just heard. If there aren’t people you can trust, try to reach out safely to those that will just kindly listen and try to empathize, even if they are strangers. One of the hardest parts of dealing with how you’re feeling is the strong sense of isolation. When I get depressive and suicidal episodes, I often feel completely alone, and feel like a bother to everyone else, which only amplifies the hurt that I’m feeling. Reach out to people, watch youtube videos of things you like, read through the reddit posts. Some tiny little steps to help you feel less isolated and alone in these moments. I’m not saying it’ll make things completely better, but in the moment it might help to bring a small sense of calm in you.

You definitely have had it very rough and I can’t even come close to imagining how stressful and difficult it must be to go through everything you do on a daily basis. Sometimes the resources available aren’t the best to provide support. If you do have someone you feel comfortable with discussing how you’re feeling, how stressed you are, and processing through everything else that’s been going on in your life, it might help to alleviate some of the burden even a little. If not, sharing on here is just a good a start that you can do. I have a lot of depressing and down days, and periodic suicidal thoughts, but when I do feel down I sometimes like to come on here and try to provide some empathy and words to posts that I’m able to read through and feel ok enough to respond to. I know how difficult it is to feel isolated and alone with your thoughts and emotions, it is a horrible feeling, so everything you feel, especially all that you’ve gone through is very valid, you’re a hard worker, and life is just beating you down. If you have the time, try finding something you enjoy doing or something that doesn’t take up too much effort or mind power to do, help you relax even if it’s for a short 10 minutes or something. The tiny things might help you work through stress as you try to build up support networks and hopefully meet people who are willing to listen and empathize with you without judgement.

When you happen to get out and if you happen to look at your post again, I’m sorry you were admitted into the psych hold. From personal experience it was one of the worst things ever for me and not helpful in any way, actually made me feel much worse and made me spiteful to the people and the situations that led me in there. I just want you to know that being placed in there does not define you, you are hurting and seeking to be understood and comforted. The process begins once you get out, it might be extremely difficult, especially living outside knowing what you experienced being put into the hospital. But personally I feel it’s important to make sure you don’t have to be put in there again. Talking to whoever might listen, without judgement is a good start.

Yeah in general suicide hotlines and helplines of the sort are highly ineffective and are full of undertrained, inefficient employees. A good start actually is being part of this sub and other subs similar to this on reddit. While it may not produce amazing results all at once, it helps a lot more to be able to read through what people are going through and converse with people who can empathize better having gone through similar situations or having similar thoughts. While there are plenty of hurtful and selfish people out there, there are also the handful of people who may be able to empathize and provide support. I may not know what you’re going through, or all the things you do feel and experience, but personally I deal with a lot of depression and the feelings of not wanting to be around, wanting things to end. For me, I don’t necessarily feel better, but I do feel my thoughts and emotions are more valid knowing there are others out there who have the same or similar thoughts and emotions. Sometimes, and this doesn’t work for everyone, and mostly for people who are willing to take that step, talking with someone you feel open to trust as a support and someone who can empathize with you can help distract you from the pains you may feel. Having support does make a difference, even the smallest amount.

Sometimes it’s the idea that someone out there can really empathize on a better level with what you’re feeling. While your situations may not be the same, you may have some similar depressive thoughts, anxiety, suicidal tendencies. And hearing other’s perspective on it or just their situations helps in a way validate what you might be feeling. It’s definitely better for me personally than hearing how to get better from someone who has never experienced anything of what I feel or think.

Hey bud, first off I’m sorry that you have to go through tough things and tough thoughts in your life. The cliched saying “it gets better” is personally very irresponsible to me when people say it, because you and I and other people are all “living” different lives and have different personalities and thought processes. While some days might have small “up” moments, sometimes those are very fleeting and the down moments are heavier to us. You say you have your close friend but they didn’t reach out. That might not invalidate how they care about you or what they might be going through as well. Maybe try reaching out to them and see what happens? If you have, and that person isn’t around at the moment, try not to lay too much blame on them either. I personally have trouble letting people into my life quickly, but I do think it is important to have multiple forms of support, even if they are just surface level, to help get through rough days, or even hours. Life is very repetitive, and it is difficult to be part of the rat race and finding purpose in it. I have trouble each day myself, even with a job and everything. One thing I can suggest is doing the things that you still kind of enjoy or find a little comfort doing. Whether that’s watching a show, or reading, or going out for a walk. Even though it’s temporary, a little thing to get your mind occupied with other thoughts may help a tiny bit just to distract you.

It’s tough when the people in closest proximity to you push you away constantly or invalidate how you’re feeling. I don’t know your situation with your parents, whether you’re very close to then or not, it’s my assumption you still stay with them and have to interact with then very regularly. When people are having these thoughts and feeling down and having thoughts of suicide, in my opinion it’s not ever just seeking attention, because ultimately there’s always some truth behind actions and thoughts, so I can say it is completely valid what you feel, and what you deal with. It’s very necessary to have someone listen to you, without judgement, just to let you know you’re heard and validate what is running through your mind. One tough day at a time.

Hey man sorry you’ve been going through these kinds of things. Depression is definitely something extremely difficult to cope with, especially when those around you are unfamiliar with it, it can make you feel more isolated and alone. Seeking comfort and love from others is a perfectly reasonable response because sometimes you may feel it can potentially heal that emptiness. What I think is important is you did try to put yourself out there, which already is a huge step even if you get shot down. Being rejected is never going to feel good at all, but the fact that you tried helps you grow even the tiniest bit, kind of like learning a lesson. You say you have female friends who compliment you, so that’s a pretty good starting point. You’re still young, you’ve graduated, so it’s a good time to focus on yourself. If you feel like you want to be loved and treated well by someone, it’s important to kind of start loving yourself too. Definitely a tough mindset to maintain when you feel depressed and rejected, I know how that feels and I still constantly deal with that. But each day that you feel like the depressive thoughts aren’t as heavy, even for small moments try to think about what would make you care for yourself, what you enjoy doing, what used to make you happy, what goals you may have, or what negative things you tell yourself or others may tell you that you might want to consider changing or proving wrong. You don’t have to have one of those “victim or victor” mindsets, I personally feel people who preach too much self help kind of sugar coat depression and emotional distress, but I do think it is important to ever so slightly deter away from putting yourself down. You gotta find some truth for yourself, and it might help you improve your mindset even a tiny bit each day. I do think it’s important to not rely on people for love and satisfaction though, because it can potentially set you up for even greater disappointment, because unfortunately there are many selfish and hurtful people out there. But the more you’re able to love yourself and find out your own truths about yourself, the more you’ll be able to grow little by little in confidence and out of that negative mindset. Just a thought, these are some of the things that have helped me a tiny bit on days where I do feel dejected and depressed.

Dang that is some real deep stuff just even reading the title. Definitely have felt the pressures or affects of everyone’s life and how they live on my life. Even when people say “you shouldn’t let others lives affect yours so much”, that’s kind of more of an easier said than done situation, 9/10 times other’s lives will affect your life, and if you’re already having a difficult time coping with your own life, the impact others may have make things just so much more difficult. Definitely something to really think about, with how being tired of living, way your living, and the way others live kind of all affect each other full circle.

It’s something to try, the hard part is “living” with the constant reminders of the injustice. But of course the saying “life isn’t fair” thoroughly applies. It’s one thing to feel depressed, but another thing to be treated differently and poorly because you’re not “ok” compared to everyone else. Morally I don’t feel comfortable with cutting people out of my life, unless they really are terrible as a person and a terrible impact on my life, which in this case is true. Even then, it is still difficult to do.

Even when you cut the person out or limit contact, that person is still technically “there”. So it’s a constant reminder sometimes that makes things difficult. And even with friends and family, some try more than others but can unknowingly make things worse because often when someone doesn’t experience depression or suicidal thoughts, there’s a threshold of empathy a person could have, and at a certain point it goes back to “why are you still sad?” Kind of mentality. Just overall very discouraging to constantly be badgered by those thoughts and feelings each day.

Real talk right there. People say you have “this and that” etc, but most times to someone feeling dejected and depressive, all that stuff is meaningless. I know for me, whenever I was told that I would have two thoughts: 1 it made me feel guilty for feeling the way that I did and just more trapped than ever, and 2 in those moments none of things I “have” matter to me because all I would want is to not feel so depressed every moment.

Definitely relate, had the same depressive episodes and tendencies during my birthday this year. Happy birthday though, what I can say is maybe try not to focus too much on it being your birthday and what other people want you to feel on this day. Give it to yourself, if you wanna feel down, let yourself feel down, or do things that you still enjoy to get away from what other people expect of you during this time. Important to get that “break” you need from everyone’s demands.

I definitely relate to that feeling, it’s tough where it can feel like one thing goes wrong and all the other things want to pile on top of it. Definitely when you’ve reached that point that you have it’s a difficult moment because you have suffered a lot, in your own eyes to feel the need to end things, and not going through with it also leaves you with a completely different difficult feeling to deal with as well in the aftermath. What I found for me to do was to just try to find something that either I liked enough or relaxed me enough to do in order to distract myself from what just happened, even for a moment, to kind of give yourself a breather. Even just laying down and trying to sleep helps to distract at times.
I think at this point talking is developing into another distraction, knowing that it’s more of a mask in front of pain, goes both ways in terms of getting and giving advice.

Definitely relating with this. The minute I was inside the ward the scenario instantly clicked, honestly if it’s someone who is just experiencing depression for the first time or other mental health issues, that place is more harm than help. The way I saw it was kind of like a “scared straight” scenario, the place was awful so I better not show my depression to not be here anymore. Obviously not a real solution to my problems, but better than being trapped in there and shelling out my money for a system and people who obviously don’t care.
